title: The hat monotile's metatile substitution as a primitive integer witness
headline: Obsmetrologia.AperiodicOrder.Tiling.Witness.hat_metatile_witness

requirements.statement: The abelianization of the metatile substitution H' = 3H + T + 3P + 3F, T' = H, P' = 2H + P + 2F, F' = 2H + P + 3F equals the matrix [[3,1,3,3],[1,0,0,0],[2,0,1,2],[2,0,1,3]] cellwise, built through StepN.substMatrix like the Fibonacci and Padovan matrices.
The matrix is nonnegative and Primitive with witness k = 2 (its square is strictly positive), through SubstitutionPrimitivity's own predicates.
The matrix is annihilated by the monic degree-4 coefficient list [-1, 7, 0, -7, 1] (x^4 - 7x^3 + 7x - 1) under StepN.evalMatPoly, and the quartic splits on the matrix as (x^2 - 7x + 1)(x^2 - 1).
The Perron factor [1, -7, 1] annihilates the fourth power of StepN.fibonacciMatrix, and does not annihilate the hat matrix alone.
The matrix is the pos-incidence projection of a FOUR-valued ChuSpace on the metatile alphabet: an entry is nonzero exactly where the relation carries positive charge.
One headline theorem bundles the paper-matrix identity, nonnegativity, primitivity, Cayley-Hamilton, and the golden factor.

prohibitions.statement: The module imports only Obsmetrologia core modules and states no real eigenvalue or eigenvector; the inflation factor phi^2 and the reflected-hat frequency are named in prose only.
The module does not claim the hat aperiodic, does not transcribe the metatile geometry or edge matching rules, and says so in a scope section of its docstring.

openQuestions.question: How does the core state the unreflected-to-reflected hat ratio phi^4 : 1 without a real Perron eigenvector — through Real.Internal or through an integer eigen-relation on the left eigenvector?

Which finite Anderson-Putnam complex of the hat (one-vertex or collared) transcribes into the JeandelRao OneVertexComplex pattern so that a nonzero H^1 class of the hat hull is exhibited as a cocycle?

references: D. Smith, J. S. Myers, C. S. Kaplan, C. Goodman-Strauss, An aperiodic monotile, Combinatorial Theory 4(1) (2024) #6, arXiv:2303.10798, section 2
M. Baake, F. Gaehler, L. Sadun, Dynamics and topology of the Hat family of tilings, arXiv:2305.05639, section 2 eq. (11) and Theorem 4

blueprint.label: thm:hat-metatile-substitution
blueprint.title: The hat metatile substitution is a primitive integer witness with golden Perron factor
blueprint.statement:
The hat metatile substitution $H'=3H+T+3P+3F$, $T'=H$, $P'=2H+P+2F$, $F'=2H+P+3F$ (Smith--Myers--Kaplan--Goodman-Strauss; the face substitution of Baake--G\"ahler--Sadun at $r=1$) abelianizes to
$M=\begin{pmatrix}3&1&3&3\\1&0&0&0\\2&0&1&2\\2&0&1&3\end{pmatrix}$.
$M$ is nonnegative and primitive ($M^2>0$), satisfies $x^4-7x^3+7x-1=(x^2-7x+1)(x^2-1)$, and its Perron factor $x^2-7x+1$ annihilates $F^4$ for the Fibonacci matrix $F$: the hat's area inflation $\varphi^4$ is the fourth rung of the metallic tower. $M$ is the $\mathrm{pos}$-incidence of a FOUR-valued Chu relation on the metatile alphabet.

frontier.label: thm:hat-reflection-frequency
frontier.title: Reflected hats have frequency $1:\varphi^4$
frontier.statement: \emph{Open frontier.} In every hat tiling the ratio of unreflected to reflected hats is $\varphi^4:1$: the left Perron eigenvector of $M$ weighted by hats per metatile $(4,1,2,2)$ against reflected hats per metatile $(1,0,0,0)$. The integer computation is $M$'s; the target is a real eigenvector witness outside the dependency-free core, or an integer eigen-relation that avoids it.

frontier.label: thm:hat-hull-cohomology
frontier.title: A finite cohomology witness for the hat hull ($\check H^1=\mathbb{Z}^4$)
frontier.statement: \emph{Open frontier.} The \v{C}ech cohomology of the hat hull is $\check H^0=\mathbb{Z}$, $\check H^1=\mathbb{Z}^4$, $\check H^2=\mathbb{Z}^{10}$ (Baake--G\"ahler--Sadun, Theorem 4). The target is a finite Anderson--Putnam complex of the hat transcribed on the Jeandel--Rao pattern, with a nonzero $H^1$ class exhibited as a cocycle and its persistence through the substitution as a chain map.
